en: And the right of your sight is that you lower it from what is not lawful for you, and that you take a lesson from what you see with it.

And the right of your legs is that you do not walk with them to what is not lawful for you. You will stand upon the Sirat (the Bridge), so take care that they do not slip with you and you fall into the Fire.
… that you guard it from unlawful intercourse and protect it from being looked at.

As for the right of prayer, it is that you know it is a coming before Allah as His guest, and that in it you are standing before Allah. When you know that, you will stand in the station of one who is lowly and humble, longing and in awe, hopeful and fearful, needy and imploring, who magnifies the One before whom he stands with stillness and dignity; and you turn to it with your heart and perform it with its limits and its rights.

And the right of your brother is that you know he is your hand, your honour and your strength. So do not take him as a weapon for disobedience to Allah, nor as a means of wronging Allah's creatures. Do not leave off helping him against his enemy, nor giving him sincere counsel. If he obeys Allah, well and good; otherwise let Allah be more honoured in your sight than he is. And there is no power except through Allah.

"… in what their souls desire they shall abide forever. The Greatest Terror shall not grieve them, and the angels shall receive them: 'This is your Day which you were promised.'" [21:102-103] O Ali, you and your Shia will be looked for at the Station (of the Gathering) while you are enjoying bliss in the Gardens. O Ali, the angels and the keepers (of Paradise) long for you, and the bearers of the Throne and the angels brought near single you out in their supplication, ask Allah out of love for you, and rejoice at whoever of them arrives among them, just as a family rejoices at an absent one who returns after a long absence. O Ali, your Shia are those who fear Allah in secret and are sincere to Him in public. O Ali, your Shia are those who compete with one another for the ranks, because they will meet Allah with no sin upon them. O Ali, the deeds of your Shia are presented to me every Friday; I rejoice at the good deeds of theirs that reach me, and I seek forgiveness for their bad deeds. O Ali, you are mentioned in the Torah, and your Shia were mentioned with every good before they were created, and likewise in the Gospel. So ask the people of the Gospel and the People of the Book; they will tell you about 'Ilya', along with your own knowledge of the Torah and the Gospel and the knowledge of the Book that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has given you. The people of the Gospel hold Ilya in great esteem though they do not know his Shia; they know them only by what they find in their books. O Ali, your companions are mentioned in heaven more greatly than the people of the earth mention them with good, so let them rejoice in that and increase in striving. O Ali, the souls of your Shia ascend to heaven in their sleep, and the angels look at them as people look at the new crescent, out of longing for them and because of the station they see them have with Allah, Mighty and Majestic. O Ali, tell your companions who recognise you to keep away from the deeds that their enemy commits, for there is no day or night but that Allah's mercy covers them; so let them avoid defilement. O Ali, the wrath of Allah is severe upon whoever detests them, disowns you and them, takes others in place of you and them, inclines to your enemy, abandons you and your Shia, chooses misguidance, wages war on you and your Shia, hates us, the Ahl al-Bayt, and hates whoever befriends you, helps you, chooses you and gives his life and wealth for us. O Ali, convey my greeting of peace to them, those whom I have not seen and who have not seen me, and let them know that they are my brothers for whom I long. Let them pass my knowledge on to those who will reach the generations after me, let them hold to the rope of Allah and cling to it, and let them strive in deeds, for we do not take them out of guidance into misguidance. Tell them that Allah is pleased with them, that He boasts of them before His angels, that He looks upon them every Friday with His mercy, and that He commands the angels to seek forgiveness for them. O Ali, do not turn away from helping a people who are told, or who hear, that I love you, and so they love you because of my love for you and hold to that as their religion before Allah, Mighty and Majestic; who have given you pure affection from their hearts, chosen you over fathers, brothers and children, and followed your path. They were made to bear hardships for our sake, yet they refused anything but to help us, and they gave their lives for us in spite of the harm and the ill words and the bitterness of it that they endure. So be merciful to them and be content with them, for Allah chose them for us by His knowledge from among creation, created them from our clay, entrusted them with our secret, bound their hearts to the recognition of our right, opened their breasts and made them hold to our rope. They do not prefer those who oppose us over us, despite what passes away from them of this world and Satan's bearing down on them with hardships. Allah has supported them and led them on the path of guidance, so they hold fast to it, while the people are in the flood of misguidance, bewildered in their desires, blind to the proof and to what has come from Allah; evening and morning they are under the wrath of Allah. But your Shia are on the way of truth and uprightness. They find no comfort in those who oppose them; the world is not of them and they are not of it. Those are the lamps in the darkness, those are the lamps in the darkness, those are the lamps in the darkness.
"… My servants", meaning Muhammad and his household, "and enter My Garden." [89:29-30] He said: Then nothing is dearer to him than the slipping away of his soul and joining the one who calls.

We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) when a man came to him and said: O Messenger of Allah, tell me about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to Iblis: "Were you arrogant, or were you among the exalted ones?" [38:75] Who are they, O Messenger of Allah, who are higher than the angels? The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: I, Ali, Fatima, Hasan and Husayn. We were in the pavilion of the Throne glorifying Allah, and the angels glorified by our glorification, two thousand years before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created Adam. When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created Adam, He commanded the angels to prostrate to him, and He did not command us to prostrate. So all the angels prostrated except Iblis; he refused and did not prostrate. Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: "Were you arrogant, or were you among the exalted ones?", meaning among these five whose names are written on the pavilion of the Throne. So we are the gate of Allah through which He is approached; through us the guided are guided. Whoever loves us, Allah loves him and settles him in His Garden; and whoever hates us, Allah hates him and settles him in the Fire. And none loves us except one whose birth is pure.
The pen has been lifted from the Shia through the protection of Allah and His guardianship.

Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, with a chain he traced back, from Abu Dawud al-A'ma, from Abu Abdullah al-Jadali, who said: Ali (peace be upon him) said: O Abu Abdullah, shall I not tell you of the good deed which, whoever brings it, is safe from the terror of the Day of Resurrection, and the evil deed which, whoever brings it, Allah throws him on his face into the Fire? He said: I said: Yes. He said: The good deed is love of us, and the evil deed is hatred of us.

And with this chain he said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: Your homes are a paradise for you and your graves are a paradise for you. For Paradise you were created, and to Paradise you will go.

O Malik, are you not pleased that you establish the prayer, pay the zakat, restrain your hands, and enter Paradise? Then he said: O Malik, there is no people who followed an imam in this world but that on the Day of Resurrection he will come cursing them and they cursing him, except you and those who are in a state like yours. Then he said: O Malik, whoever of you dies upon this matter is a martyr, in the position of one who strikes with his sword in the way of Allah. He said: And Malik said: One day while I was sitting with him and was thinking to myself about something of their merit, he said to me: By Allah, you are our Shia; do not think that you are going too far regarding us. O Malik, no one is able to describe Allah; and just as no one is able to describe Allah, so no one is able to describe the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family); and just as no one is able to describe the Messenger, so no one is able to describe us; and likewise no one is able to describe the believer. O Malik, the believer meets his brother and shakes his hand, and Allah keeps looking at them while sins fall away from their faces until they part; and no one is able to describe one who is like this. And he said: My father (peace be upon him) used to say: The Fire will never consume one who professes this matter.

"I know a people whom Allah has forgiven, with whom He is pleased, whom He has protected, shown mercy to, guarded from every evil, supported, guided to every right course, and brought to the utmost of what is possible." It was said: Who are they, O Abu Abdullah? He said: "Those are our righteous Shia, the Shia of Ali (peace be upon him)."

Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us; he said: Ya'qub ibn Yazid narrated to us … from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad al-Qibti, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) say: The people neglected the words of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) about Ali (peace be upon him) on the day of Ghadir Khumm, just as they neglected his words on the day of the upper room of Umm Ibrahim. The people came to visit him in his illness, and Ali (peace be upon him) came to draw near to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) but found no place. When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saw that they were not making room for Ali (peace be upon him), he said: O people, these are my household; do you slight them while I am alive among you? By Allah, if I am absent, Allah is not absent from you. Ease, comfort, good pleasure, glad tidings, love and affection are for whoever follows Ali as his imam, takes him as his master, and submits to him and to the successors after him. It is a duty upon me to include them in my intercession, because they are my followers. "Whoever follows me is of me" [14:36], an example that applied to me from Ibrahim, because I am of Ibrahim and Ibrahim is of me; my religion is his religion, my way is his way, his merit is my merit, and I am more excellent than he; and my merit is a merit for him, confirming the word of my Lord: "Offspring, one of the other; and Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing." [3:34] (The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had been laid up because of his leg in the upper room of Umm Ibrahim when the people visited him.)

I heard a saying narrated from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), that he said: The fortunate one is he who was fortunate in his mother's womb, and the wretched one is he who was wretched in his mother's womb. The fortunate one is he who takes a lesson from others. The shrewdest shrewdness is God-consciousness, and the most foolish foolishness is wickedness. The worst narration is the narration of lies, and the worst of matters are those newly invented. The worst blindness is blindness of the heart. The worst regret is when death comes to one of you, and the greatest regret is the regret of the Day of Resurrection. The greatest wrong in the sight of Allah is a lying tongue. The worst earning is the earning of usury, and the worst eating is consuming the property of the orphan unjustly. The best adornment of a man is good conduct together with faith; it is what most governs his affair, and the mainstay of his affair is how it ends. Whoever seeks to be heard of, Allah will expose him. Whoever puts his trust in this world will fall short of it. Whoever recognises trial bears it patiently, and whoever does not recognise it recoils. Doubt is unbelief (the text of this book reads "sin"; the other books that carry this sermon read "doubt"). Whoever is arrogant, Allah brings him low. Whoever obeys Satan disobeys Allah; whoever disobeys Allah, He punishes him; and whoever thanks Him, He gives him more. Qasim said in his narration: Whoever is patient in a calamity, Allah gives him something good in its place. Whoever relies on Allah, Allah is enough for him. Do not anger Allah to please any of His creatures, and do not draw near to any creature by moving away from Allah, for there is nothing between Allah and any of His creatures by which He gives him good or wards off evil from him except obedience to Him. Obedience to Allah is success in every good that is sought and deliverance from every evil that is feared. Allah protects whoever obeys Him and does not protect whoever disobeys Him. One who flees from Allah finds no place to flee to. The command of Allah comes down as it is, even if creatures dislike it. Everything that is coming is near. What Allah wills comes to be, and what He does not will does not come to be. Help one another in righteousness and God-consciousness, and do not help one another in sin and aggression; and be mindful of Allah, for Allah is severe in punishment. [5:2]
… Allah, Blessed and Exalted: "They give what they give while their hearts are fearful" [23:60]. He said: He does what people do while he is fearful and hopeful.

Abu Abdullah told me of his son Isma'il's dutifulness to him and said: I already loved him, and he has increased in my love. A foster-sister of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) came to him. When he saw her he was delighted with her, spread out his cloak for her and seated her on it; then he turned to her, talking with her and smiling at her. Then she rose and left. Then her brother came, and he did not treat him as he had treated her. It was said: O Messenger of Allah, you did for his sister what you did not do for him, and he is a man. He said: Because she was more dutiful to her father than he was.

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) say: A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said: O Messenger of Allah, I have relatives with whom I kept ties, yet they harm me, and I intend to cast them off. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to him: Then Allah will cast all of you off. He said: What should I do? He said: Give to the one who deprives you, keep ties with the one who cuts you off, and pardon the one who wrongs you. If you do that, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will be a supporter (zahir) for you. Abdullah ibn Talha said: I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): What is the zahir? He said: The helper.

Fadala ibn Ayyub narrated to us, from Mu'awiya ibn Ammar, from Amr ibn Ikrima, who said: I came to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and said to him: I have a neighbour who harms me. He said: Be merciful to him. I said: May Allah not have mercy on him. He turned his face away from me. I did not like to leave it there, so I said: He does things to me and harms me. He said: Tell me, if you confronted him openly, would you get your due from him? I said: Yes, I would get the better of him. He said: This one is among those who envy people for what Allah has given them of His bounty. When he sees a blessing upon someone, if he has a family he turns his affliction on them; if he has no family he turns it on his servant; and if he has no servant he lies awake at night and seethes by day. A man of the Ansar came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said: O Messenger of Allah, I have bought a house among the Banu so-and-so, and my nearest neighbour is one whose good I do not hope for and from whose evil I am not safe. He said: So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered Ali, Salman and Abu Dharr (he said: and I have forgotten one, I think it was Miqdad) to call out in the mosque at the top of their voices: There is no faith for one whose neighbour is not safe from his harm. They called it out three times. Then he ordered it to be announced that every forty houses in front of him, behind him, to his right and to his left, their residents are his neighbours.

Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him); he said: I heard him say: The likeness of this world is that of a snake: its touch is soft and inside it is deadly poison. The man of sense is wary of it, while children reach for it with their hands.

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): I would not be pleased to have the world and all it contains in exchange for your right. He said: Fie on the world and what is in it! And what is it, O Dawud? Is it anything but two garments and the filling of your belly?

I was sitting with the Commander of the Faithful (the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him) when a man came to him, complained to him of the world and condemned it. The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to him: The world is an abode of truth for one who is truthful with it, an abode of wealth for one who takes provision from it, and an abode of good outcome for one who understands it. It is the place of prostration of Allah's loved ones, the place where Allah's revelation descended, the place of prayer of His angels and the marketplace of His friends; in it they earned Paradise and gained mercy. So why do you condemn it? It has announced its parting, called out that it will end, and announced the death of itself and its people. By its trials it gave a likeness of the trial to come, and by its joys it made them long for the joy to come. It leaves in the evening with a calamity and comes in the morning with well-being, as a warning, an encouragement and a cause for fear. So some men condemn it on the morning of regret, and others praise it: it reminded them and they took heed, it spoke to them and they believed. O you who condemn the world while taken in by its deception: when did the world earn your blame, and when did it deceive you? Was it by the resting places of your fathers in the earth, or by the beds of your mothers in decay? How many have you nursed with your own hands, and how many have you tended, seeking a cure for them and asking the physicians to prescribe for them? Your concern did not benefit him, and what you sought was not granted. Through him the world showed you your own self, and through his death your own death. So it befits you that your weeping over it should not come to an end, when you know that your loved ones will not avail you.

Jabir narrated to me; he said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to me: O Jabir, regard this world as a lodging where you have stopped and then mean to move on from that very day, or like wealth you gained in your sleep and then woke with none of it in your hand. When you are at a funeral, be as though you were the one being carried, and as though you had asked your Lord to return you to the world so that you might do the deeds of one who lives. For this world, in the eyes of those who know, is like a shadow.

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) say: A man came in to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) while he was on a mat that had left marks on his body, with a pillow of palm fibre that had left marks on his cheek. He began to wipe them and say: Neither Khosrow nor Caesar would be content with this. They sleep on silk and brocade, and you are on this mat? The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: I am better than both of them, by Allah; I am more honoured than both of them. By Allah, what have I to do with this world? The likeness of this world is that of a rider who passed by a tree that had shade, so he rested in its shade; when the shade moved away he set off, went on and left it.

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) said to me: Never have two matters come before me, one for this world and the other for the Hereafter, and I chose this world, but that I saw what I disliked before evening. Then Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said of the Umayyads: They have been preferring this world to the Hereafter for eighty years, and they see nothing that they dislike.
The two angels write down only what the servant utters.

… Allah, Blessed and Exalted: "When the two receivers receive, seated on the right and on the left" [50:17]. He said: They are the two angels. And I asked him about the words of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: "This is what is with me, ready" [50:23]. He said: He is the angel who keeps the record of his deeds against him. And I asked him about the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "His companion will say: Our Lord, I did not make him transgress" [50:27]. He said: He is a devil.
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: (It used to be said that) among the servants of Allah most beloved to Allah is the doer of good who repents often.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Dawud (peace be upon him): Go to My servant Daniyal and say to him: You disobeyed Me and I forgave you; you disobeyed Me and I forgave you; you disobeyed Me and I forgave you. If you disobey Me a fourth time, I will not forgive you. So Dawud (peace be upon him) came to him and said: O Daniyal, I am the messenger of Allah to you, and He says to you: You disobeyed Me and I forgave you; you disobeyed Me and I forgave you; you disobeyed Me and I forgave you. If you disobey Me a fourth time, I will not forgive you. Daniyal said to him: You have conveyed it, O prophet of Allah. When it was the time before dawn, Daniyal rose and called upon his Lord in private, saying: O Lord, Dawud Your prophet has told me from You that I disobeyed You and You forgave me, I disobeyed You and You forgave me, I disobeyed You and You forgave me; and he has told me from You that if I disobey You a fourth time You will not forgive me. By Your might and Your majesty, if You do not protect me, I will surely disobey You, and then disobey You, and then disobey You.

Muhammad ibn Sinan narrated to us, from Ammar ibn Marwan, who said: I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) say: From you, by Allah, it is accepted, and for you, by Allah, there is forgiveness. Nothing stands between one of you and his being delighted and seeing joy and the comfort of his eyes except that his soul reaches here, and he pointed with his hand to his throat. Then he said: When that happens and he is at the point of death, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), the Imams, Ali, Jibra'il and the Angel of Death (peace be upon him) attend him. Jibra'il (in another reading: Ali, peace be upon him) draws near to him and says to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): This one used to love you (in another reading: love us), the Ahl al-Bayt, so love him. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) says: O Jibra'il, this one used to love Allah, His Messenger and the family of His Messenger, so love him and be gentle with him. (And Jibra'il says to the Angel of Death: This one used to love Allah, His Messenger and the household of His Messenger, so love him and be gentle with him.) Then the Angel of Death draws near to him and says: O servant of Allah, have you taken the release of your neck? Have you taken the guarantee of your acquittal? Did you hold fast to the greatest protection in the life of this world? He said: Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, grants him success (in another reading: raises him) and he says: Yes. He says to him: And what is that? He says: The wilayah of Ali ibn Abi Talib. He says: You have spoken the truth. As for what you used to fear, Allah has made you safe from it; and as for what you used to hope for, you have attained it. Receive glad tidings of the righteous predecessors: the company of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), Ali (and Fatima) and the Imams from his descendants (peace be upon them). Then he draws out his soul gently. Then his shroud is brought down from Paradise, and his embalming scent, a scent like pungent musk. He is shrouded (in that shroud) and embalmed with that scent, then clothed in a yellow robe from the robes of Paradise. (When he is placed in his grave, Allah opens for him one of the gates of Paradise,) and its comfort and fragrance enter upon him. (Then space is made for him in front of him to the distance of a month's journey, and to his right and to his left. Then it is said to him: Sleep the sleep of a bride on her bed. Receive glad tidings of comfort and fragrance, a garden of bliss, and a Lord who is not angry. (Then he visits the family of Muhammad in the gardens of Radwa; he eats with them of their food, drinks with them of their drink, and talks with them in their gatherings until our Qa'im, of the Ahl al-Bayt, rises. When our Qa'im rises, Allah raises them and they come with him answering the call, group after group. At that time the followers of falsehood will doubt, and those who make lawful what is forbidden will dwindle away, and few they will be. Those who hasten ahead perish and those who are brought near are saved. For this reason the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to Ali (peace be upon him): You are my brother, and the meeting place between me and you is Wadi al-Salam.) He said: And when the unbeliever is at the point of death, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), Ali, the Imams, Jibra'il (and Mika'il) and the Angel of Death (peace be upon them) attend him. Jibra'il (in another reading: Ali, peace be upon him) draws near to him and says: O Messenger of Allah, this one used to hate you, the Ahl al-Bayt, so hate him. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) says: O Jibra'il, this one used to hate Allah, His Messenger and the household of His Messenger, so hate him (and be harsh with him). And Jibra'il says: O Angel of Death, this one used to hate Allah, His Messenger and the household of His Messenger, so hate him and be harsh with him. Then the Angel of Death draws near to him and says: O servant of Allah, have you taken the release of your pledge (in another reading: your neck)? Have you taken the guarantee of your acquittal (from the Fire)? Did you hold fast to the greatest protection in the life of this world? (He says: No.) He says: Receive tidings, O enemy of Allah, of the wrath of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, His punishment and the Fire. As for what you used to hope for, it has passed you by; and as for what you used to fear, it has come down upon you. Then he draws out his soul harshly. Then three hundred devils are put in charge of his spirit, all of them spitting in his face, and he is tormented by its smell (in another reading: by his spirit). When he is placed in his grave, one of the gates of the Fire is opened for him, and (the blast of its wind,) its pus and its flame enter upon him.

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): What is the meaning of the words of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: "Why then, when it reaches the throat, while you at that time look on, and We are nearer to him than you, but you do not see; why then, if you are not to be held to account, do you not bring it back, if you are truthful?" [56:83-87] He said: When the soul of the dying person reaches the throat, and he was a believer, he sees his place in Paradise and says: Return me to the world so that I may tell its people what I see. It is said to him: There is no way to that.

It is said to the believer in his grave: Who is your Lord? He says: Allah. It is said to him: What is your religion? He says: Islam. It is said: Who is your prophet? He says: Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). It is said: Who is your Imam? He says: Ali (peace be upon him). (It is said: How did you come to know that? He says: It is a matter to which Allah guided me and on which He made me firm.) (It is said to him: Sleep a sleep without dreams, the sleep of a bride. Then a gate to Paradise is opened for him, and its comfort and fragrance enter upon him.) He said: Then he says: O Lord, hasten the coming of the Hour for me, that I may return to my family and my wealth. He said: And it is said to the unbeliever: Who is your Lord? He says: Allah. It is said to him: Who is your prophet? He says: Muhammad. It is said to him: What is your religion? He says: Islam. It is said: From where did you come to know that? He says: I heard the people saying it, so I said it. (It is said to him: Who is your guardian (wali)? He says: I do not know.) Then the two of them strike him with a mace which, if humans and jinn together gathered against it, they could not bear. He said: He melts as lead melts. Then they return the spirit to him, and his heart is placed between two plates of fire, and he says: O Lord, delay the coming of the Hour.

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) said to me: On the Day of Resurrection Allah will gather all creatures, the first and the last, on a single plain. Then a caller will call: Where are the people of merit? He said: A group of people will rise, and the angels will meet them and say: What was your merit? They will say: We used to keep ties with those who cut us off, give to those who deprived us, and pardon those who wronged us. They will say: Enter Paradise. Then a caller will call: Where are the neighbours of Allah in His abode? Another group of people will rise, and the angels will say to them: By what did you become neighbours of Allah? They will say: (We used to hasten to one another for the sake of Allah,) hate for the sake of Allah, love one another for the sake of Allah, and (share with one another) give freely to one another for the sake of Allah (and hold one another to account for the sake of Allah, and bless one another for the sake of Allah). Then a caller will call: Where are the people of patience? He said: A group of people will rise, and the angels will meet them and say: In what were you patient? They will say: We were patient in obedience to Allah, and we held ourselves back from disobeying Him. It will be said to them: Enter Paradise.

Jibra'il (peace be upon him) came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), took him by the hand and led him out to al-Baqi'. He came to a grave and called out to its occupant: Rise, by Allah's permission. He said: A man with a bright white face came out of it, wiping the dust from his face and saying: Praise be to Allah, and Allah is greatest. Jibra'il said: Return, by Allah's permission. Then he took him to another grave, called out to its occupant and said to him: Rise, by Allah's permission. A man with a blackened face came out of it, saying: Alas, my sorrow! Alas, my ruin! Then (Jibra'il) said (to him): Return (to what you were), by Allah's permission. Then he said: O Muhammad, this is how they will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection: the believers will say these words, and these others will say what you have seen.

Allah sent to the Children of Israel a prophet called Irmiya (Jeremiah) and said: Say to them: What of a land, among the noblest of lands, in which I planted the noblest of plants and which I cleared of every foreign growth, yet it turned out otherwise and grew carob? (They laughed at him and mocked him, so he complained of them to Allah, and Allah revealed to him: Say to them:) The land is Bayt al-Maqdis and the plants are the Children of Israel. I cleared them of every foreign element and removed every tyrant from them, yet they turned out otherwise and committed acts of disobedience. So I will surely give power over them, in their own land, to one who will shed their blood and take their wealth. (If they weep I will not have mercy on their weeping, and if they call on Me I will not answer their call. They have failed and their deeds have failed, and) I will surely lay it waste for a hundred years, and then I will surely rebuild it. He said: When he told them, the scholars were distressed and said: O messenger of Allah, what is our sin, when we did not do as they did? Go back to your Lord on our behalf. So he fasted seven days, and nothing was revealed to him. He ate a meal, then fasted seven days. When it was the twenty-first day, Allah revealed to him: You shall stop what you are doing, coming back to Me about a matter I have already decreed, or I will turn your face to your back. Then He revealed to him: Say to them: You saw wrong and did not denounce it. And He gave Bukht Nassar (Nebuchadnezzar) power over them, and he did to them what has reached you.

Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Khalid al-Maraghi informed me; he said: Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi narrated to us; he said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Marwan al-Ghazzal narrated to us; he said: My father narrated to us; he said: Ubayd ibn Khunays al-Abdi narrated to us; he said: Sabbah ibn Yahya al-Muzani narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Sharik, from al-Harith ibn Tha'laba, who said: Two men arrived, heading for Mecca and Medina, at the new moon or before the new moon, and found the people setting out for the Hajj. He said: [They said:] So we set out with them, and we came upon a group of riders among whom was a man who seemed to be their leader. He drew apart from them and said: You must be Iraqis. We said: We are Iraqis. He said: You must be Kufans. We said: We are Kufans. He said: From whom are you? We said: From the Banu Kinana. He said: From which of the Banu Kinana? We said: From the Banu Malik ibn Kinana. He said: Welcome upon welcome, and nearness upon nearness. I adjure you by every revealed Book and every prophet sent: have you heard Ali ibn Abi Talib insult me, or say that I am an enemy to him and one who fights him? We said: Who are you? He said: I am Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas. We said: No, but we heard him say: "Beware of the trial of al-Ukhaynis." He said: Those called Khunays are many; but did you hear him mention me by my name? They said [We said]: No. He said: Allah is greatest, Allah is greatest! Then I would have gone astray and would not be among the guided if I were to fight him after four things that I heard from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) about him; to have just one of them would be dearer to me than the world and all that is in it, with the lifespan of Nuh to live in it. We said: Name them [for us]. He said: I mentioned them only because I want to name them. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent Abu Bakr with (Surah) Bara'a to proclaim it to the polytheists. When he had travelled for a night or part of a night, he sent Ali ibn Abi Talib after him and said: Take Bara'a from him and send him back to me. So the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) went to him, took Bara'a from him and sent him back to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). When he stood before him (peace be upon him), he wept and said: O Messenger of Allah, has something happened concerning me, or has Quran been revealed about me? The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "No Quran has been revealed about you, but Jibra'il (peace be upon him) came to me from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and said: None shall convey on your behalf except you or a man from you. Ali is from me and I am from Ali, and none shall convey on my behalf except Ali." We said to him: And what is the second? He said: We were in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), along with the family of Ali, the family of Abu Bakr, the family of Umar and his uncles. He said: Then it was called out among us at night: Leave the mosque, except the family of the Messenger of Allah and the family of Ali. He said: So we went out dragging our belongings. When morning came, his uncle Hamza came to him and said: O Messenger of Allah, you have put us out and let this youth stay, while we are your uncles and the elders of your family?! The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: "It was not I who put you out, nor I who let him stay; rather Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded me to do that." We said to him: And what is the third? He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent his banner to Khaybar with Abu Bakr, and he brought it back; then he sent it with Umar, and he brought it back. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) became angry and said: "Tomorrow I will give the banner to a man whom Allah and His Messenger love and who loves Allah and His Messenger, one who attacks again and again and does not flee; he will not return until Allah grants victory at his hands." He said: When morning came we knelt up on our knees, but we did not see him call any of us. Then he called out: Where is Ali ibn Abi Talib? He was brought, and his eyes were inflamed. He put his saliva in his eye and gave him the banner, and Allah granted victory at his hands. We said: And what is the fourth? He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) set out on the expedition to Tabuk and left Ali in charge of the people. Quraysh envied him and said: He only left him behind because he disliked his company. He said: So he set off after him until he caught up with him, took hold of the stirrup of his she-camel and said: I am following you. He said: What is the matter with you? He wept and said: Quraysh claim that you only left me behind because you dislike me and dislike my company. He said: So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ordered his caller, who called out among the people, and then he said: O people, is there any one among you who does not have someone especially close among his family? They said: Indeed. He said: Then Ali ibn Abi Talib is the one especially close among my family and the beloved of my heart. Then he turned to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said to him: Are you not pleased to be to me as Harun was to Musa, except that there is no prophet after me?! Ali (peace be upon him) said: I am pleased with Allah and His Messenger. Then Sa'd said: These are four, and if you wish I will tell you a fifth. We said: We do wish it. He said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) on the Farewell Pilgrimage. When he was returning he stopped at Ghadir Khumm and ordered his caller, who called out among the people: "Whoever I am the master (mawla) of, this Ali is his master. O Allah, befriend whoever befriends him, be the enemy of whoever is his enemy, help whoever helps him, and forsake whoever forsakes him."

Musa ibn Imran had a brother in Allah whom Musa used to honour, love and esteem. A man came to that brother and said: I would like you to speak for me to this tyrant; and the tyrant was one of the kings of the Children of Israel. He said: By Allah, I do not know him and have never asked him for anything. He said: What harm is there in that for you? Perhaps Allah (Majestic is His Majesty) will fulfil my need at your hand. So he felt pity for him and went with him without Musa's knowledge. He came to him and entered. When the tyrant saw him he brought him close and honoured him. He asked him for the man's need and he fulfilled it for him. Before long that tyrant was struck down and died. The people of his kingdom gathered for his funeral, and the doors of the markets were closed for his death so that people could attend it. And it was decreed that the believing young man, the brother of Musa, died on the day that tyrant died. When the brother of Musa entered his house he would lock his door, and no one could reach him; when Musa wanted him he would open the door and go in to him. Musa forgot him for three days. On the fourth day Musa remembered him and said: I have left my brother for three days and not gone to him. He opened the door and went in to him, and found the man dead, and the creatures of the earth had crept over him and eaten from the fair features of his face. When Musa saw him so, he said: O Lord! For Your enemy You gathered the people, and Your friend You caused to die and then set the creatures of the earth upon him to eat from the fair features of his face? Allah (Majestic is His Majesty) said: O Musa, My friend asked this tyrant for a need and he fulfilled it for him. So I gathered the people of his kingdom to pray over him, to repay him on the believer's behalf for fulfilling his need, so that he would leave the world with no good deed left with Me for which I would reward him. And as for this believer, I set the creatures of the earth upon him to eat from the fair features of his face because he asked that tyrant, which was not pleasing to Me, so that he would leave the world with no sin against him with Me.

… it, He would give it to him and that would not diminish His kingdom at all; but if he asked Him for the space of his foot of this world, He would deny him. And the unbelieving servant is of so little account to Allah (Majestic is His Majesty) that if he asked Him for this world and all it contains He would give it to him, and that would not diminish His kingdom at all; but if he asked Him for the space of his foot of Paradise, He would deny him. And Allah (Majestic is His Majesty) looks after His believing servant with trials as a man looks after his family with gifts, and He guards him as the physician guards the sick.

And from him (peace be upon him), he said: The Lord looks after the believer. Forty mornings do not pass him by but that He attends to him, either with an illness in his body, or with an affliction in his family and wealth, or with one of the afflictions of this world, so that Allah may reward him for it.

And from him (peace be upon him), he said: The believer does not escape one of three things, or all three may be brought together upon him: someone with him in his own house who shuts his door on him, or a neighbour who harms him, or someone on his way to his needs who harms him. Even if a believer were on a mountain peak, Allah would send a devil to trouble him; and Allah makes for him, out of his faith, a companion.

And from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah (Majestic is His Majesty) says: O world, pass over My believing servant with all kinds of trials in his worldly affairs, tighten his livelihood for him, and do not be sweet to him lest he settle into you.
I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) say: If you want to be my brothers and my companions, then prepare yourselves for enmity and hatred from people; otherwise you are not companions of mine.

And from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: How wonderful is the case of the believer! Allah decrees nothing for him but that it is good for him: if he is tried he is patient, and if he is given he is thankful.

And from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said: When the believing servant does good, Allah multiplies his deed for him, seven hundredfold for every deed. That is the word of Allah (Majestic is His Majesty): "The likeness of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is that of a grain that grows seven ears, in every ear a hundred grains. Allah multiplies for whom He wills, and Allah is All-Embracing, All-Knowing." [2:261]

I came to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) having been thinking to myself about certain things. He said to me: O Malik, think well of Allah, and do not think that you are going too far in your matter. O Malik, you are not able to describe the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and likewise you are not able to describe us, and likewise you are not able to describe the believer. O Malik, the believer meets his brother and shakes his hand, and Allah (Majestic is His Majesty) keeps looking at them while sins fall away from their faces until they part with no sin upon them. So how can you describe one who is like this?

I shared a mount with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) to Mecca. When he dismounted he would shake my hand, and when he mounted he would shake my hand. I said: May I be your ransom, it is as though you see something in this? He said: Yes. When the believer meets his brother and shakes his hand, they part without any sin.

Allah (Majestic is His Majesty) says: Whoever humiliates a friend of Mine has lain in wait to make war on Me, and I am the swiftest of all in helping My friends. I have not hesitated over anything I do as I hesitate over the death of My believing servant: I love to meet him and he dislikes death, so I turn it away from him. He asks of Me and I give him; he calls on Me and I answer him. If there were none in the world but one believing servant, I would have no need, with him, of all My creation, and I would make for him out of his faith a companion, so that he would not feel lonely for anyone.

And from Abu al-Samit, he said: I came to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and he said: O Abu al-Samit, rejoice, then rejoice, then rejoice! Then he said to me: O Abu al-Samit, Allah (Majestic is His Majesty) forgives the believer even if he comes with the like of this and the like of this (and he pointed to the domes. I said: Even if he comes with the like of those domes? He said:) Yes, by Allah, even if it were the like of those domes. Yes, by Allah.

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): What is the right of the believer over the believer? He said: I am concerned for you; I fear that you will know and not act, and neglect it and not keep it. He said: I said: There is no might and no power except through Allah. He said: The believer has seven obligatory rights over the believer, and there is not one of them but that it is obligatory on his brother. If he neglects one of them he leaves the guardianship (wilayah) of Allah and abandons obedience to Him, and he has no share in it. The easiest of them is that you love for him what you love for yourself and dislike for him what you dislike for yourself. The second is that you help him with your self, your wealth, your tongue, your hands and your feet. The third is that you follow what pleases him, avoid what angers him and obey his command. The fourth is that you be his eye, his guide and his mirror. The fifth is that you are not full while he is hungry, nor quenched while he is thirsty, nor clothed while he is unclothed. The sixth is that if you have a servant and he has none, and you have a wife who looks after you and he has no wife to look after him, you send your servant to wash his clothes, prepare his food and make his bed. The seventh is that you fulfil his oath, accept his invitation, visit him when he is ill and attend his funeral; and if he has a need, you hasten to fulfil it and do not make him ask you for it. If you do that, you have joined your wilayah to his and his wilayah to yours. And from al-Mu'alla the like of it; in his narration he said: If you do that, you have joined your wilayah to his wilayah and his wilayah to the wilayah of Allah (Majestic is His Majesty).

I was with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), I and Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur and Abdullah ibn Talha. He (peace be upon him) said, without being asked: O Ibn Abi Ya'fur, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: There are six qualities; whoever has them will be before Allah (Majestic is His Majesty) and at the right of Allah (Majestic is His Majesty). Ibn Abi Ya'fur said: What are they, may I be your ransom? He said: That a Muslim loves for his brother what he loves for the dearest of his family, dislikes for his brother what he dislikes for the dearest of his family, and is sincere to him in friendship. Ibn Abi Ya'fur wept and said: How is he sincere to him in friendship? He said: O Ibn Abi Ya'fur, when he is in that position with him, he shares his cares with him: he is concerned for his concern, glad for his gladness when he is glad, and sad for his sadness when he is sad. If he has something to relieve him, he relieves him; otherwise he prays to Allah for him. He said: Then Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: Three are for you and three are for us: that you recognise our merit, that you follow in our footsteps, and that you await our outcome. Whoever is like this will be before Allah, and those below them will take light from their light. As for those at the right of Allah, if those below them could see them, life would not be pleasant for them because of the merit they would see in them. Ibn Abi Ya'fur said: Why do they not see them, when they are at the right of Allah? He said: O Ibn Abi Ya'fur, they are veiled by the light of Allah. Has the narration not reached you that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to say: The believers are at the right of Allah and before Allah; their faces are whiter than snow and brighter than the midday sun. Someone will ask: Who are these? It will be said: These are the ones who loved one another for the sake of the majesty of Allah.

We asked him about a man who has only his day's food, while among them is one who has a month's food and one who has a year's food: should the one with a day's food show kindness to one who has nothing, the one with a month's food to one who has less, and the one with a year's food to one who has less, in that manner, all of that being the sufficiency for which one is not blamed? He (peace be upon him) said: They are two matters. The best of you in it is the one keenest in desire for it and in preferring others over himself. Allah (Majestic is His Majesty) says: "They prefer others over themselves, even though they are in need" [59:9]. Otherwise, he is not blamed for it. The upper hand is better than the lower hand, and one begins with those he supports.

And from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he said to Abu Isma'il: O Abu Isma'il, tell me, among the people where you are, when a man has no cloak and one of his brothers has a spare cloak, does he give it to him until he gets a cloak? He said: I said: No. He said: And when he has no waist-wrap, does one of his brothers send him a waist-wrap until he gets one? I said: No. He struck his thigh with his hand and said: These are not brothers.

Any believer who relieves a believer of a distress, Allah relieves him of seventy distresses of this world and of the Day of Resurrection. He said: Whoever makes things easy for a believer who is in difficulty, Allah makes easy for him the needs of this world and the Hereafter. Whoever conceals a believer's fault, Allah conceals seventy of his faults that he leaves behind in this world and the Hereafter. He said: And Allah is helping the believer as long as the believer is helping his believing brother. So benefit from the admonition and desire what is good.

And from a man of Hulwan, who said: I was circling the House when a man from among our companions came and asked me for a loan of two dinars. I had done five circuits, so I said to him: Let me finish my seven, then I will come out. When I began the sixth, Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) leaned on me and put his hand on my shoulder. He said: I completed my seven and went into another because Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) was leaning on me. Each time I came to the Corner the man gestured to me. Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: Who is this gesturing to you? I said: May I be your ransom, this is one of your followers who asked me for a loan of two dinars; I told him: I will finish my seven and come out to you. He said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) pushed me away and said: Go and give them to him. I thought he said "give them to him" because I had said I had agreed to it. The next day I came to him while several of our companions were with him and he was speaking to them. When he saw me he broke off and said: To walk with a brother of mine in a need until I fulfil it for him is dearer to me than freeing a thousand slaves and sending out a thousand horses, saddled and bridled, in the way of Allah.

I heard al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say: Whoever relieves a believer of one of the distresses of this world, Allah relieves him of one of the distresses of the Hereafter, and he will come out of his grave with a heart at ease.
Whoever relieves his Muslim brother of a distress, Allah will relieve him of a distress on the Day of Resurrection.

Among what Allah said in intimate address to His servant Musa ibn Imran was: I have servants to whom I give free use of My Garden and whom I give authority in it. Musa said: O Lord, who are these to whom You give free use of Your Garden and authority in it? He said: Whoever brings joy to a believer. Then he said: A believer lived in the kingdom of a tyrant who was set on harming him, so he fled from him to the land of polytheism and stayed with a man of the polytheists, who was kind to him, treated him gently and gave him hospitality. When death came to that man, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to him: By My might and My majesty, if there were a dwelling in My Garden for a polytheist I would have settled you in it; but it is forbidden to whoever dies a polytheist. But, O Fire, keep him and do not harm him. He said: And his provision is brought to him at both ends of the day. I said: From Paradise? He said: Or from wherever Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wills.

And from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said: Whoever brings joy to a believer, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, creates a creature that meets him at his death and says to him: Rejoice, O friend of Allah, in honour from Allah and His good pleasure. Then it stays with him until he enters his grave and says the like to him; and it stays with him at every terror, giving him glad tidings and saying the like to him. He says to it: Who are you, may Allah have mercy on you? It says: I am the joy that you brought to so-and-so.

I was with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) on the Day of Tarwiya when Maymun al-Qaddah came in and complained to him that he could not find a mount to hire. He said to me: Get up and help your brother. I went out with him, and Allah made the hire easy for him. I returned to my place and he said to me: What did you do about your Muslim brother's need? I said: Allah the Exalted fulfilled it. He said: Indeed, your helping your brother is dearer to me than a tawaf of seven circuits of the Ka'ba. Then he said: A man came to al-Hasan ibn Ali (peace be upon them both) and said: May my father and mother be your ransom, O Abu Muhammad, help me with my need. He put on his sandals and went with him. He passed by al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon them both), who was standing in prayer, and said to the man: Why did you not go to Abu Abdullah and ask his help with your need? He said: I did, and I was told that he was in i'tikaf. He said: If he had helped you with your need it would have been better for him than a month's i'tikaf.

A man's walking for the need of his Muslim brother: ten good deeds are written for him, ten bad deeds are erased from him, he is raised ten degrees, and it equals freeing ten slaves; and it is better than a month's i'tikaf in the Sacred Mosque with its fasting.
And from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), he said: Whoever walks for a need of his Muslim brother until he completes it, Allah will make his feet firm on the day when feet slip.

And from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever helps his anguished, distressed brother out of a grief or hardship, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, writes for him seventy-two mercies; He gives him one of them at once, by which He sets right his worldly affairs, and seventy-one for the terrors of the Hereafter.
And from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever honours a believer is honouring Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

And from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said: In fulfilling a man's need for his Muslim brother there are three things: doing it quickly, making little of it, and keeping it concealed. When you do it quickly you make it pleasant; when you make little of it you have made it great; and when you conceal it you have safeguarded it.

And from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said: Any believer who gives a believer a loan seeking the face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Allah writes its reward for him as charity is reckoned. And there is no believer who prays for his brother in his absence but that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, appoints an angel who says: And for you the like of it. And he (peace be upon him) said: The prayer of a believer for a believer wards off trial from him and brings provision flowing to him.

I was in the tawaf when Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) took me by the upper arm, greeted me and said: Shall I not tell you of the merit of tawaf around this House? I said: Yes. He said: Any Muslim who circles this House seven times, then comes to the Station and prays two rak'ats behind it, Allah writes for him a thousand good deeds, erases from him a thousand bad deeds, raises him a thousand degrees and confirms for him a thousand intercessions. Then he said: Shall I not tell you of something better than that? I said: Yes. He said: Fulfilling a person's need is better than a tawaf of seven circuits, and seven, until he reached ten. Then he said: O Ibrahim, a believer gains no gain more harmful to him than wealth that he acquires. Wealth is more harmful to him than two ravenous wolves among sheep whose shepherds have perished, one at their front and the other at their rear. Then he said: What do you think of the two? I said: They will ruin them, may Allah keep you well. He said: You have spoken the truth. The least that comes upon him is that his Muslim brother comes to him and says: Give me in marriage, and he says: You have no wealth.

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the right of the believer over the believer. He said: The right of the believer is greater than that; if I told you of it you would disbelieve. When the believer comes out of his grave, a form comes out of his grave with him and says to him: Rejoice in honour from your Lord and in joy. He says to it: May Allah give you good tidings. Then it goes on with him, giving him the like of those tidings. And he narrated it from another, who said: When he passes a terror, it says: This is not for you; and when he passes something good, it says: This is for you. It stays with him, making him safe from what he fears and giving him tidings of what he loves, until he stands before Allah, Mighty and Majestic. When he is ordered to Paradise, the form says to him: Rejoice in Paradise, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has ordered you to Paradise. He says to it: Who are you, may Allah have mercy on you? You gave me good tidings when I came out of my grave, kept me company on my way and told me about my Lord. It says: I am the joy that you used to bring to your brothers in the world. I was made from it to help you and to keep you company in your loneliness.

And from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Dawud (peace be upon him): A servant of Mine comes to Me with a good deed and I give him free use of My Garden. Dawud said: O Lord, what is that good deed? He said: He brings joy to My believing servant, even if with a single date. Dawud said: It befits one who knows You not to cut off his hope in You.
And from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said: When a Muslim's Muslim brother comes to him and he goes with him in his need, he is like one who strives in the way of Allah.

And from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said: Whoever helps his believing brother who is distressed and anguished in his hardship, relieving his distress and helping him to achieve his need, has for that seventy-two mercies from Allah, Mighty and Majestic; He gives him one of them at once, by which He sets right the matter of his livelihood, and stores up for him seventy-one mercies for the terrors of the Resurrection and its horrors.

Any believer who visits a sick person for the sake of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wades deep into mercy, and when he sits with him he is immersed in it. If he visits him in the morning, seventy thousand angels pray for him until evening; and if he visits him in the evening, seventy thousand angels pray for him until morning.

And from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said: Any believer who visits his believing brother in his illness, seventy-seven thousand angels pray for him. When he sits with him mercy covers him, and they seek forgiveness for him until evening. If he visits him in the evening, he has the like of that until morning.

And from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), he said: When a Muslim servant leaves his house intending to visit his brother for Allah and not for anything else, seeking the face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and desiring what is with Him, Allah appoints seventy thousand angels who call to him from behind until he returns to his home: You have done well, and Paradise is good for you.

And from the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), that he said to one of his companions: Will you come with us to visit so-and-so in his illness? He said: So I went with him, and there was Abu Musa al-Ash'ari sitting with him. The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: O Abu Musa, have you come to visit a sick man or simply to visit? He said: To visit the sick. He said: Indeed, when a believer visits his sick believing brother, seventy thousand angels pray for him until he returns to his family.

Jibra'il (peace be upon him) told me that Allah sent an angel down to the earth. That angel walked on until he came to the door of a man's house, where a man was asking permission to enter upon the owner of the house. The angel said to him: What do you need from the owner of the house? He said: He is a Muslim brother of mine whom I am visiting for the sake of Allah. He said: Did nothing but that bring you? He said: Nothing but that brought me. He said: I am the messenger of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to you. He sends you greetings of peace and says: I have made Paradise due to you. He said: And the angel said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: Any Muslim who visits a Muslim is not visiting him; he is visiting Me, and his reward is Paradise.

And from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Shall I not tell you of your men who are among the people of Paradise? They said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: The prophet, the truthful one, the martyr, the newborn child, and the man who visits his brother at the far side of the town, visiting him only for the sake of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

I heard the Righteous Servant say: Whoever visits his believing brother for Allah and not for anything else, seeking by it the reward of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the fulfilment of the promises of Allah the Exalted, Allah appoints seventy thousand angels, from the time he leaves his house until he returns to it, who call to him: You have done well, and Paradise is good for you; you have taken a dwelling in Paradise.
And from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said: Whoever visits his believing brother, the Lord, Majestic is His Majesty, says: O visitor, you have done well, and Paradise is good for you.

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Any Muslim who visits a sick person from among the believers wades through the sands of mercy. When he sits with him, mercy covers him. When he returns, seventy thousand angels escort him until he enters his home, all of them saying: You have done well, and Paradise is good for you.

And from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), he said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has a garden that none enter but three: a man who judges against himself with the truth, a man who visits his believing brother in kindness, and a man who is good to his believing brother for the sake of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

And from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdullah (peace be upon them both), they said: On the Day of Resurrection the believing servant will be brought to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and He will call him to an easy account. Then He will reproach him and say to him: O believer, what kept you from visiting Me when I was ill? The believer will say: You are my Lord and I am Your servant. You are the Living One whom no pain or weariness touches. The Lord, Mighty and Majestic, will say: Whoever visits a believer in his illness has visited Me. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will say: Do you know so-and-so, son of so-and-so? He will say: Yes. He will say to him: What kept you from visiting him when he was ill? Had you visited him you would have visited Me; then you would have found Me there when you asked; then had you asked Me for a need I would have fulfilled it for you, and I would not have turned you away from it.

And from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): An angel passed by a man standing at the door of a house. The angel said to him: O servant of Allah, what keeps you standing at the door of this house? He said: A brother of mine is inside it, and I wanted to greet him. The angel said: Is there close kinship between you and him, or has some need drawn you to him? He said: No. There is no kinship between me and him and no need has drawn me to him, only the brotherhood of Islam and its sanctity. So I look in on him and greet him for the sake of Allah, the Lord of the worlds. The angel said to him: I am the messenger of Allah to you. He sends you greetings of peace and says to you: It was Me you intended and to Me you were coming. I have made Paradise due to you, freed you from My anger and protected you from the Fire.

And from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), he said: Any believer who visits a believer is a visitor of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. And any believer who visits a sick believer wades deep into mercy. When he sits, mercy covers him. When he leaves, Allah appoints seventy thousand angels who seek forgiveness for him, ask for mercy on him and say: You have done well, and Paradise is good for you, until that hour of the next day; and he has a kharif of Paradise. The narrator said: What is the kharif, may I be your ransom? He said: A corner of Paradise in which a rider travels for forty years.
Feeding four Muslims until they are full equals freeing a slave from the descendants of Isma'il (peace be upon him).
And from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said: No believer brings two believers into his house and feeds them until they are full but that it is better than freeing a slave.

Whoever feeds a believer in hunger, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will feed him from the fruits of Paradise. Whoever gives a believer drink in thirst, Allah will give him to drink on the Day of Resurrection from the sealed nectar. Whoever clothes a believer in his nakedness, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will clothe him in green garments. And in another narration he said: Whoever clothes a believer in his nakedness remains under the guarantee of Allah as long as a thread of it is on him.

And from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said: Whoever feeds a believer in hunger, Allah will feed him from the fruits of Paradise. Any believer who gives a believer drink, Allah will give him to drink from the sealed nectar. And any believer who clothes a believer in his nakedness remains under the cover and protection of Allah as long as a scrap of it remains.

And from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), that he said to one of his companions: O Thabit, can you not free a slave every day? (He said:) May Allah keep you well, I am not able to do that. He said: Are you not able to give four Muslims a morning or an evening meal? I said: That I am able to do. He said: By Allah, it equals freeing a slave.

And from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said: Whoever clothes a believer with a garment remains in the mercy of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, as long as anything of the garment remains. Whoever gives him a drink of water, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will give him to drink from sealed nectar. And whoever satisfies his hunger, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will feed him from the fruits of Paradise.

And from the Commander of the Faithful Ali (peace be upon him), that he said: To feed your brother a morsel is dearer to me than giving a dirham in charity; to give him a dirham is dearer to me than giving ten in charity; and to give him ten is dearer to me than freeing a slave.

And from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said: No believer feeds a believer until he is full but that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, feeds him from the fruits of Paradise; nor gives him a drink but that Allah gives him to drink from the sealed nectar; nor clothes him with a garment but that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, clothes him in green garments, and he is under the guarantee of Allah the Exalted as long as a thread of that garment remains.

And from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), he said: Among the qualities most beloved to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, are three: a Muslim who feeds a Muslim in hunger, or relieves him of a distress, or pays a debt for him.
And from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said: The first gift given to the believer in his grave is that those who followed his funeral are forgiven.

And from Sadir, he said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: What prevents you from freeing a slave every day? I said: My wealth cannot bear that. He said: Then feed a Muslim man every day. I said: A well-off one or a poor one? He said: The well-off one may also crave food.
And from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he said: Feeding a Muslim equals freeing a slave.

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) say: The nearest a servant comes to unbelief is when a man is another man's brother in religion and then keeps a record of his slips and stumbles in order to bring him down one day.

And from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said: Whoever slanders a believing man or woman with what is not in them, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will raise him in the clay of khabal until he comes out of what he said. I said: What is the clay of khabal? He said: Pus that comes out of the private parts of prostitutes.

And from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), he said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever spreads an indecency is like the one who began it, and whoever shames a believer for something will not die until he commits it.

I said to Abu Abdillah (a.s.): My master has property in my hands, so I asked him to make lawful for me the slave-girls I buy. He said: "If it is lawful for me to make it lawful for you, then it is lawful for you." So I asked Abu Abdillah (a.s.) about that, and he said: "If he makes a particular slave-girl lawful for you, she is lawful for you. But if he says, 'Buy whichever of them you wish,' then do not approach any of them except the one he directs you to, unless it is a slave-girl he sees and says, 'She is lawful for you.' And if you have property of your own, then buy with your own property whatever you see fit."

…a man who deflowered his girl, meaning his wife, and caused her a tearing injury (ifda). He said: The blood-money (diyah) is due from him if he consummated with her before she reached nine years. He said: If he then keeps her and does not divorce her, nothing is due from him. And if he consummated with her when she was nine years old, nothing is due from him; if he wishes he keeps her, and if he wishes he divorces.

Regarding a man who bought a slave-girl who had not menstruated, he said: If she is young and pregnancy is not feared for her, there is no waiting period upon her on his account, and he may approach her if he wishes. But if she has reached maturity and has not menstruated, then the waiting period is upon her. He said: And I asked him about a man who bought a slave-girl while she was menstruating. He said: When she becomes pure, he may touch her if he wishes.

…of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "There is no secret counsel of three but He is their fourth, nor of five but He is their sixth, nor of fewer than that nor more but He is with them wherever they may be. Then on the Day of Resurrection He will inform them of what they did. Indeed Allah knows all things." (58:7) He said: This verse was revealed about so-and-so and so-and-so, Abu Ubaydah al-Jarrah, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, Salim the client of Abu Hudhayfah and al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, when they wrote the document among themselves and made a pact and agreed that if Muhammad passed away, the caliphate would never be among the Banu Hashim, nor the prophethood. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse about them. He said: I said: His words, Mighty and Majestic: "Or have they settled upon a plan? Then We too are settling. Or do they think that We do not hear their secret and their private counsel? Yes indeed, and Our messengers are with them, writing." (43:79-80) He said: These two verses were revealed about them on that day. Abu Abdillah (a.s.) said: Do you suppose there was any day like the day the document was written, other than the day al-Husayn (a.s.) was killed? So it was in the prior knowledge of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, which He made known to the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.): that when the document was written, al-Husayn would be killed and the rule would leave the Banu Hashim. And all of that came to pass. I said: "And if two parties of the believers fight, make peace between them; but if one of them transgresses against the other, fight the one that transgresses until it returns to the command of Allah; and if it returns, make peace between them with justice." (49:9) He said: The two parties: the realisation of this verse came on the day of Basra, and they are the people of this verse. They are the ones who transgressed against the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.), so it was obligatory on him to fight them and kill them until they returned to the command of Allah. Had they not returned, it would have been obligatory on him, according to what Allah revealed, not to lift the sword from them until they returned and went back on their opinion, because they had pledged allegiance willingly, not under compulsion. They are the transgressing party, as Allah the Exalted said. So it was obligatory on the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) to act justly towards them once he had prevailed over them, just as the Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.a.) acted justly towards the people of Mecca: he showed them favour and pardoned them. Likewise the Commander of the Faithful (a.s.) did with the people of Basra when he prevailed over them, the same as the Prophet (s.a.w.a.) did with the people of Mecca, step for step. He said: I said: His words, Mighty and Majestic: "And the overturned city He brought down." (53:53) He said: They are the people of Basra; it is the overturned one. I said: "And the overturned cities; their messengers came to them with clear proofs." (9:70) He said: Those are the people of Lut; it was overturned upon them, turned upside down upon them.

…the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of night and day are signs for those of understanding (190), those who remember Allah standing, sitting and on their sides, and reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth: "Our Lord, You did not create this in vain. Glory be to You; so protect us from the punishment of the Fire (191). Our Lord, whomever You admit to the Fire, You have disgraced him, and the wrongdoers have no helpers (192). Our Lord, we heard a caller calling to faith, 'Believe in your Lord,' so we believed. Our Lord, forgive us our sins, remove from us our misdeeds and take us with the righteous (193). Our Lord, grant us what You promised us through Your messengers and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed You do not break the promise (194)." Looking into the well of Zamzam removes illness, so drink of its water from the side next to the corner in which the Black Stone is, for beneath the Stone are four rivers of Paradise: the Euphrates, the Nile, Sayhan and Jayhan, and these two are rivers. A Muslim should not go out to jihad with one who cannot be trusted in judgement and does not carry out the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, regarding the spoils (fay'). If he dies in that, he has been a helper to our enemy in withholding our rights and shedding our blood, and his death is a death of the Age of Ignorance. Remembering us, the Ahl al-Bayt, is a cure for ailments, sicknesses and the whispering of doubt, and turning towards us is the pleasure of the Lord, Mighty and Majestic. The one who holds to our cause will be with us tomorrow in the Sacred Precinct. The one who awaits our cause is like one weltering in his blood in the way of Allah. Whoever was present with us in our war, or heard our call for help, and did not help us, Allah will cast him on his face into the Fire.
